newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds firm, depos, drachma up in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds firm, depos, drachma up in thin volume.

text.p: Greek depos were firmer a tenth of a point, forex forwards were biased upwards, bond yields fell on local buying and the drachma advanced against the ecu in thin trading with U.S. markets closed for Independence Day, dealers said.
"Depos are up about 10 basis points across-the-board in subdued trading," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Forex forwards are little changed but most deals have been on the offer side."
Bonds added to their earlier gains with bids of 10-year bonds around 97.90. Three- and five-year bonds also advanced on buying mainly from local players.

"Bonds had hit a bottom, discounting a lot of bad news and it was natural to correct," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Yields of three-, five-and 10-year bonds have fallen on buying interest from local investors."
The National Statistics Service announced that CPI-based inflation firmed to 5.5 percent year-on-year in June from 5.4 percent in May.
The mark was quoted at 157.35/45 from Friday's 157.425 fix, the dollar at 275.66/76 drachmas from 275.500 and the ecu at 309.64/74 from 309.80 drachmas.

"Ecu/drachma has eased, trading around the lower end of its intraday range of 309.70-309.98," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "With U.S. markets closed, it was expected to see thin trading in forex markets."
